mechanism_narrative: The steep fall in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last two weeks will continue to suppress discretionary foot traffic, so RETAIL_REC will stay below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below their current four-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls below -50 percent and WORKPLACES remains below -35 percent, the implied access constraint reduces mall and shopping-district visits within one week, pushing RETAIL_REC further down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50 and WORKPLACES stays below -35
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -55.4 at t-0w and WORKPLACES is -40.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES cross the stated thresholds together.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home, which reduces spontaneous shopping trips and depresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower two weeks ahead whenever RESIDENTIAL remains elevated relative to the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with a less negative TRANSIT reading signals renewed trip-making and corridor activity, which spills over into retail visits with about a two-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -19.3 at t-2w to -2.9 at t-1w before weakening again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after PARKS rises and TRANSIT becomes less negative together.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns negative while PARKS stays subdued, households are likely shifting from routine out-of-home errands to fewer discretionary trips, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops below 0 while PARKS stays below 0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is -4.4 at t-0w and PARKS is -15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS remaining below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp worsening in TRANSIT relative to WORKPLACES signals commuting disruption that quickly cuts incidental retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should fall within one week of the worsening gap.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines faster than WORKPLACES by at least 10 points in a week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -41.0 to -55.4 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall in the week after TRANSIT deteriorates at least 10 points faster than WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL continues rising above 20 percent while RETAIL_REC remains below -50 percent, the city is still in an effective stay-at-home regime and retail visits will remain depressed for the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 20 while RETAIL_REC stays below -50
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 21.0 at t-0w and RETAIL_REC is -52.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds to above its last-28-day mean within four weeks even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 and RETAIL_REC remains below -50 at the trigger point.

mechanism_narrative: An early recovery in GROCERY_PHARM followed by stabilization in WORKPLACES predicts that essential-trip normalization is preceding broader discretionary reopening, which lifts RETAIL_REC after about four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near zero or slightly positive through t-1w before turning negative at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes and WORKPLACES stops falling.
